rows.Description: Let's begin by setting up the ipsilateral and contralateral femoral access.
Ultrasound-guided retrograde bilateral femoral access. 6Fr introducer, double Proglide prepositioning per side, 10 Fr sheath.
rows.Notes: Suitable navigational wires, eg, J-tip guidewires, advanced into the abdominal aorta.

rows.Description: Insert the standard guidewire from the left access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: guidewire; required_stiffness: standard; access_scope: left
rows.Notes: Keep left and right access distinct until the stiff guidewire establishes the ipsilateral side. Left/right pairs need not occur in the printed order; the stiff-wire access establishes the ipsilateral side.

rows.Description: Insert the standard guidewire from the right access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: guidewire; required_stiffness: standard; access_scope: right
rows.Notes: Keep left and right access distinct until the stiff guidewire establishes the ipsilateral side. Left/right pairs need not occur in the printed order; the stiff-wire access establishes the ipsilateral side.

rows.Context / Step: Catheter insertion and advancement via the Ipsilateral Side
rows.Description: A suitable catheter (eg, Berenstein) is passed over the ipsilateral J-tip wire and the two are advanced into the thoracic aorta to ensure non-traumatic access.First guidewire into the thoracic aorta, then catheter.
rows.Notes: IMPLEMENTATION GAP: this step permits a suitable catheter (e.g. Berenstein), whereas A-M03/A-M04 currently require pigtail or marker pigtail on both sides.

rows.Description: A pigtail catheter is inserted via the contralateral femoral artery and over the J-tip wire and positioned with the tip curled just above the renal artery level (usually just above the L1-L2 disc space).
